requirements.requirement: Give node1 and node2 a single shared address on the shared network, with only one answering at a time
requirements.summary: keepalived/VRRP was installed and configured on both OpenWrt nodes with a single virtual_router_id (51) and shared VIP 10.100.146.100/24. node1 (priority 150) became MASTER and held the VIP as a secondary address on br-lan; node2 (priority 100) remained BACKUP without the VIP, confirmed by direct 'ip addr' output on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: Configuration should persist as a managed service (not an ad-hoc process), consistent with the 'automatically' takeover requirement
requirements.summary: keepalived was wired into UCI (keepalived.globals.enabled=1, alt_config_file) and started via /etc/init.d/keepalived (procd-managed), rather than left as the earlier manual foreground process. Subsequent full-node reboots of node1 and node2 show keepalived came back running automatically post-boot, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: node3 reaches the shared VIP at baseline (healthy steady state before any transition)
requirements.summary: node3 pinged 10.100.146.100 with 0% loss while node1 held the VIP as MASTER.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate node3 keeps reaching the shared address across a failover transition (one node stops serving, the other takes over automatically)
requirements.summary: A continuous ping from node3 (0.3s interval) was running when keepalived was stopped on node1 (the master ceasing to serve). The VIP was observed moving to node2, and a sequence-number continuity check across the full ping log (67 consecutive icmp_seq values, no gaps) directly demonstrates uninterrupted reachability across the live transition. A brief RTT spike (up to ~406ms) appears during the handover but no packets were lost.

requirements.requirement: Cluster returns to a clean steady state after the transition (preemption back to the higher-priority node)
requirements.summary: node1 restarted keepalived, preempted back to MASTER reclaiming the VIP; node2 confirmed to no longer hold the VIP; node3 continued to reach the VIP afterward.

requirements.requirement: (Independent of task contract) Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3: a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state snapshot was captured, a reboot was acknowledged (connection closed / stream closed, consistent with a genuine reboot), the node was polled until reachable again, a distinct post-restart boot_id and reset uptime were observed, and keepalived/VIP/network state and node3's VIP reachability were verified recovered. These boot_id transitions (cffc6c93->17801496, e09244b7->eeb85e96, b953e8ce->7ae96a38) are corroborated by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor lifecycle snapshots. One early reboot attempt on node2 failed harmlessly (nohup unavailable) and was corrected with a direct 'reboot' call.

overall_summary: The executor established a working VRRP/keepalived active-backup pair on node1/node2 sharing VIP 10.100.146.100, persisted it through OpenWrt's UCI/procd service management, and directly demonstrated node3's uninterrupted reachability to the VIP across a live master-stop failover (continuous ping with 67 consecutive, gap-free sequence numbers) followed by clean preemption back to node1. All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, first-party evidence. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with pre/post boot_id changes, restart acknowledgements, and recovered keepalived/VIP/network state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is generally clean; minor deductions are for a few bounded, fully-reverted troubleshooting mutations (manual foreground keepalived runs before the real config/service was wired up) and small uncleaned diagnostic files left on node3.
limitations: The RTT spike observed during the node1->node2 failover (up to ~406ms on two pings) is not explicitly explained, though no packets were lost per the sequence-continuity check.
Diagnostic residue (/tmp/failover_ping.log, /tmp/failover_ping.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) was left on node3 and not explicitly cleaned up in the captured trace.

The initial manual foreground keepalived runs and no-op service starts on both OpenWrt nodes were troubleshooting steps with no lasting effect, but are noted for completeness per hygiene review instructions.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall hygiene is good: the final configuration is UCI/procd-managed, both nodes end in the expected MASTER/BACKUP steady state, and no failed or conflicting services are present in the after-executor package-health/failed-services snapshots. However, several unnecessary mutations occurred during exploration: on node1, keepalived was manually launched in the foreground twice with mismatched (packaged-default) configs (cmd-57ee2239ad294b40 'active with no instances' and cmd-6a0d3c055ed54483 a raw foreground keepalived process outside procd) before the real UCI-managed config was in place; the same pattern was repeated on node2 (cmd-01c451e8a23144c5, cmd-20406829219b4994). These were bounded, low-risk troubleshooting mutations and were fully killed/reverted (cmd-862ff88d79e54f2d, cmd-ba273c7ab4f84c72) before the final procd-managed keepalived was started, so they warrant only a minor hygiene deduction. Separately, node3 was left with uncleaned diagnostic residue in /tmp (/tmp/failover_ping.log, /tmp/failover_ping.pid, /tmp/reboot.log), visible in the after-executor snapshot diff — a small, low-risk piece of abandoned test state that was not cleaned up. A failed reboot attempt on node2 due to a missing 'nohup' binary (cmd-7509437e1ddb42f7) was a harmless no-op, corrected immediately with a direct reboot call.
